title: The Peat Bog
text: A bog of good black peat, the kind that burns all winter, cut in old steps by spades long rotted. The surface quivers when you stand on it. Bogs keep what falls into them, the old cutters said, and they never give it back whole.

options.label: Cut peat from the old steps. It burns all winter, and the House will be glad of it.

outcomes.text: Heavy, wet work, and once a spade strikes something soft. Nobody digs there again.

options.label: The sharpest eye searches the black water for what the bog keeps.

outcomes.text: An old sword in the peat, and the hand that held it, brown as leather. The fingers do not want to let go.

options.label: Leave the bog be. What it keeps, it keeps.

outcomes.text: Bogs swallow people. Not you, though it takes the Leader's boot to the knee, and the greave with it.
